$comment: Single source of truth for the immutable refs that ci.yml and release.yml pin each sibling backend checkout to (§17 pin B). Each pinned commit CONTAINS the committed contract artifacts the gen:* drivers regenerate from: docs/schema.json, docs/flows.json, docs/errors.json, docs/capabilities.json (+ pyproject.toml for the manifest backend-version pin). Bumping a pin is a deliberate PR after the backend releases a new contract — never float main. Procedure: CONTRIBUTING.md, section 'Contract pins'. 2026-07-16: bumped to the v1-canon-sweep release tags (§60, api-versioning.md) — auth v0.5.8, notifications v0.3.8, profiles v0.3.13, billing v0.4.11, workspaces v0.4.2, calendar v0.3.4, recordings v0.3.2; all contracts now carry /<mod>/api/v1/ paths; react gen:* artifacts regenerated against these refs in the same change. 2026-08-09: the Spanish wave — auth v0.20.1, notifications v0.7.1, billing v0.6.1, workspaces v0.22.1 bumped to the releases that carry translations/errors.es.json (profiles was already there; calendar and recordings ship no locale catalogues at all and are deliberately left behind, so their pairs stay en-only rather than gaining a fabricated empty one). Each note below states what the bump drags in BESIDES the catalogue. 2026-08-23: stapel-video v0.7.0 joins the pins — the first entry added FOR a pair rather than under one: nothing in this repo read stapel-video before, and the release that gave ParticipantSpan a scope_key is the only reason @stapel/video-react exists. It is also the first pin whose gen:errors runs with ERRORS_CATALOG_DIR pointed at stapel-core (the module ships no translations/ of its own). 2026-08-23: stapel-billing v0.6.1 -> v0.8.1 — the wallet body grows lots[], holds[] and expiring_soon, which is the whole reason @stapel/billing-react's useWallet and its new /default <WalletPanel/> exist; the same span prunes the core-owned error keys out of billing's own translations/, so the ru/es bundles now depend on the stapel-core merge that was already in place.

What the span DOES carry, and why the pin moves anyway: 0.51.0 adds stapel_core.sites - one host registry that ALLOWED_HOSTS, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, the WebSocket origin allowlist, auth's return_to allowlist and the storefront brand all derive from (STAPEL_SITES, the 17th extension point in docs/capabilities.json, which is the only committed contract artifact this bump changes); 0.52.0 adds the stapel_lifecycle E001 adoption check - an app subscribing to user.deleted without a user.merged handler now fails manage.py check, a backend-side finding no React pair can answer but one that gates the siblings this repo pins; 0.52.1 is 0.52.0 with docs/capabilities.json regenerated (the version bump had shipped without make contract); 0.53.0 parks ValidationError instead of retrying it forever - deliver_to_subscribers() counts an unprocessable payload into bus_dlq_total{reason="unprocessable"} and acks it, and bus.dlq.REASONS gains "unprocessable". stapel-chat.note: release v0.7.3 - 2026-08-30: the presence deadline reaches the client. ParticipantResponse gains `online_until` and chat.presence.changed carries it too. It exists because a lease running out announces NOTHING - a flip is announced from a disconnect, and the lease is for the case where no disconnect ever runs - so a client told only `online: true` believed it forever after a peer's tab was killed. Observed live on a stand: a header said online 90s after the peer was gone while the server already said offline. This is the pin <PresenceLine/>'s local expiry timer regenerates against; still absent from the schema's `required` list, so the pair reads a 0.7.0 body unchanged. release v0.7.0 - 2026-08-30: presence stops being the reader's own socket. ParticipantResponse gains `online` and `last_seen_at` (both OPTIONAL in the schema's required list, so a host still on 0.6.x sends a body without them and the pair reads that as "offline, nothing to say" rather than as a broken contract), and chat.presence.changed joins the conversation stream. This is the pin @stapel/chat-react's <PresenceLine/> and participantPresence() regenerate against; without it the generated Participant type has no presence fields and the header falls back to the transport tag that caused the bug. release v0.6.3 - 2026-08-28: consumes user.merged, so a guest's conversations survive signing in. Carries v0.6.2 (E017 names the floor and says it cannot see a stale remote peer over the bus) and v0.6.1 (a block refuses the THREAD, not only the message, while existing history still returns). release v0.6.0 — 2026-08-26: chat-react regenerated against the released tag (0.6.1 tagged, not on PyPI yet). release v0.2.2 — the ref that finally EXPORTS the socket: routing.py mounts stapel_chat.consumers.ChatConsumer at ws/chat/<uuid:conversation_id>, so the resumable protocol the consumer had always implemented (hello{last_seq} -> welcome -> replay -> replay_done -> live message frames, seq-dedup, error{resync} past REPLAY_LIMIT=500) is reachable by a host for the first time. That is why @stapel/chat-react ships two transports behind one seam instead of the polling-only v1 the storefront spec assum

stapel-search.note: release v0.14.0 - 2026-09-03: the pin moves because the pair must render a wire that now tells the three empty-panel cases apart. A UX walker measured the filter sheet printing «Для этого поиска фильтров нет» on /c/telefony (46 listings), /c/elektronika (52) and ?q=iPhone (14) against 12 groups on the single leaf /c/mobilnye-telefony — forty-six phones that all carry a manufacturer, under the words 'no filters'. The cause was the PLAN, not the counting: facet_plan asks categories.features for ONE category and that Function resolves own + ANCESTOR-inherited features, so a branch owns no axes (its leaves do) and a text query names no category at all — the same deployed server, asked explicitly with &facets=vendor, answered apple 13 / samsung 10 / xiaomi 9 on the branch. 0.14.0 draws the plan from the categories the candidate set actually contains (the new OPTIONAL backend verb category_counts, one grouped aggregate over the same predicate facets() counts through), ranks them by predicted coverage with _facet_rank unchanged as the tie-break, and withholds a borrowed slug with thin support. facet_meta gains three fields the pair READS rather than merely tracks: `plan` (category | evidence), `withheld` ({slug, coverage, candidates} — «no filters for this search» is FALSE whenever this is non-empty, which is precisely the lie the pair was rendering), and `categories` ({category, count} for the categories the result set is made of, busiest first, the same slash-joined id path the category filter already takes — the material the panel needs to offer the CATEGORY as the first filter on a text search). degraded[] gains facet_plan_evidence for an engine that cannot aggregate. Without `withheld` the panel cannot tell 'nothing to offer' from 'offered nothing because it would apply to too few of these'. release v0.10.1 - 2026-09-02: the pin catches up with the contract the pair's own committed manifest already declares (>=0.10 <0.11) - search-react 0.17.0 was regenerated against the 0.10 wire and the pin was left at 0.9.0, so gen:manifest:check regenerated the OLD range on the runner and main went red on a stamp no local gate disagreed with. One pin, one manifest, one claim. release v0.9.0 - 2026-09-02: the pin catches up with what the fleet installs. facet_meta gains `dropped_filters` — the `f.`/`r.` filters an answer did NOT apply because the category marks the slug non-public — which is the field @stapel/search-react's panel must not silently swallow, and the reason the pair is regenerated here rather than left describing a 0.7.0 wire. release v0.7.0 - 2026-08-31: the TYPE-AHEAD offers categories, with the result list's own counts. `GET /suggest` gains `categories[]` - the full ancestor path, the number of live listings behind it, and a `category` string ready to paste straight into the SERP's filter, ranked by that number. It is the answer to a query whose right answers are not strings: a leaf like "shorts" sits under men's, women's and children's clothing at once, and until now /suggest answered listing titles only. The count is the SERP's own - the module's suite asks it for the count and asks /query for the same category and fails if the two differ - and it is one aggregate over the index rather than a query per path. This is the contract the pair's type-ahead reads, and it is what closes 'a search cannot reach a category' without the frontend building a second, count-less ranking of its own. The pin is also what the classified fleet installs. release v0.6.0 - 2026-08-31: a VOCABULARY-backed facet gets captions too, which is the half of the slug-on-screen defect 0.4.0 left open. 0.4.0 captioned the slugs whose options are inline in the category config; a live classified deployment then showed a phone panel reading a captioned condition directly above three raw storage slugs for manufacturer, model and memory size - and those are the rows a phone buyer actually filters on. 0.6.0 resolves those captions AFTER the count, through stapel-attributes' vocabulary resolver (facets.vocabulary_labels), one batched call per slug: it cannot happen in the plan, because a catalogue level holds tens of thousands of terms and the plan does not know which of them a query will produce. An unresolved code is ABSENT from the map rather than echoed, so the pair can tell "no caption" from "the caption is the slug". No resolver registered, or one that raises: the answer is exactly what it was - a caption is never a precondition for answering. 0.5.0 in the same span adds the cross-script reach as a CONFORMANCE scenario (a normalizer that expands correctly into an engine that ignores the expansion answers the same wrong number, which is how a shipped ru dictionary sat unused since 0.1.0 with every unit test over it green); no runtime behaviour, but a third-party backend must now pass one more scenario. This is also the version the classified fleet installs, so the pair is regenerated against the contract it will meet. release v0.4.0 - 2026-08-31: r.price is a CORE range field (index_schema.CORE_RANGE_FIELDS -> price_base), announced per answer in facet_meta.core_ranges - the panel offers a price filter without keeping its own list of which slugs are core. facet_labels ships each select option's caption beside its count ({slug: {translatable, values}}), so a SERP rendered from the search answer alone stops printing storage slugs at buyers; a vocabulary-backed slug is absent rather than guessed at. degraded[] is deduplicated across layers and phrase_synonyms is reported per ANSWER (a multi-word group member) rather than per engine class - Postgres now declares phrase_synonyms because phraseto_tsquery is the adjacency the capability names. The envelope also states the `language` whose dictionary answered. release v0.3.1 - 2026-08-30: floor stapel-attributes>=0.5, contract regen. get_facet_mapping answers 'term' for ref_select and 'path' for ref_hierarchical_select, and closed_options is not built for any config carrying an optionsRef - a vocabulary is open to the planner, so its zero buckets are not enumerable. release v0.2.2 — 2026-08-24 pair wave: the pair regenerated schema/errors against this contract. release v0.2.0 — the count contract. The 0.1.0 answer could say `count: 0` next to a non-empty items[] (the Postgres typo fallback answered from the trigram arm while the total kept counting the tsquery arm that had just found nothing), and this pair printed it as «Примерно 0 объявлений» over the visible cards. 0.2.0 makes `count` NULLABLE, adds `count_is_lower_bound: bool` (a floor — render "N+"), and redefines `exact_total` as a property of THIS answer rather than of the engine class, with `degraded: ["exact_total"]` following it. That is the whole reason for the bump: @stapel/search-react 0.4.0 renders the three states (exact / floor / unknown) and stops raising a degradation banner for an `exact_total`-only degradation, which is a count nuance and not a failed search. stapel-listings.note: release v0.21.0 - 2026-09-03: the pin moves because the pair is about to CONSUME the 0.20.0 contract, not merely to be current. `models.OWNER_TRANSITIONS`, `POST listings/{id}/transition/` and `available_transitions` on the owner card are the server's answer to «there is no way back»: before them the owner API exposed only `archive` and `complete`, both exits, so a cabinet could offer a seller nothing but DELETE out of SOLD, ARCHIVED, PAUSED or EXPIRED. The dashboard now renders the moves the server reports instead of re-deriving a state machine it cannot see. 0.21.0 rides along and is read-side only: the public card coarsens `lat`/`lon` to ~1.1km, blanks `geohash` and adds `geo_precision_km`, while the OWNER's read (the one `fromDetail` loads a draft from) still carries the exact point — so the composer does not move a listing a kilometre per save. release v0.19.0 - 2026-09-03: the pin catches up with what the fleet actually runs, and the delta is checked rather than assumed. `git diff v0.17.0..v0.19.0` over the CONTRACT is three `pattern` constraints on `category_id` in docs/schema.json (an id must look like an id) and nothing else; translations/ is byte-identical across the span, so every ru/es bundle regenerates unchanged. stapel-geo.note: release v0.4.1 - 2026-08-30: adds GET /geo/api/v1/ip, the centre a map opens on before the browser's position prompt is answered - or after it is refused, which is a supported answer and not an error. The verb ALWAYS answers something a map can open on: an unknown range, a private address, a missing database or a provider that raised all come back 200 with the deployment fallback centre and ip_resolved:false, and only a deployment with no locator answer AND no fallback centre answers 204. That shape is why geo-react useResolvedLocation can be a three-rung ladder (browser fix -> IP city -> configured centre) with one branch instead of an error path. map/config.endpoints gained "ip", so the pair still learns every path from the server. Behind it: the IP_LOCATORS merge-registry (offline MaxMind via the stapel-geo[ipgeo] extra, or a single configured static point), and IP_TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH / IP_CLIENT_IP_RESOLVER, which count X-Forwarded-For from the RIGHT so a caller-forged prefix cannot pick its own city. Checks W008/W009/W010. 2026-08-26: geo-react ships ru+es locale bundles. release 0.4.0 - the release that made a location a HUMAN thing and the only reason @stapel/geo-react can exist. Until 0.4.0 the module shipped coordinates and called it a feature, which is how a live listing composer ended up with two raw fields named latitude and longitude; 0.4.0 adds GET map/config (public - the tile layer, its ATTRIBUTION OBLIGATION, the search discipline, and the endpoint table a client is asked to read its four other paths from) and GET geocoding/resolve (one round trip: display line, address components, alternatives, geohash, opt-in nearest Location rows), which are the two calls the default picker is built on. What is read here: docs/schema.json (12 paths under /geo/api/v1/, 12 component schemas - MapConfig, TileLayer, GeocodeResponse/Feature/Geometry/Properties and PlaceResolution/PlaceSummary are the ones this pair generates against), docs/errors.json (50 codes: 8 owned by stapel_geo, 42 cross-cutting stapel_core) and pyproject.toml 0.4.0 -> backend.contract >=0.4 <0.5. docs/flows.json carries two flows (geo.pick_location, geo.geocode_address); the pair drives the pick from a bag rather than a flow machine, because the steps are a finger on a map and a browser permission prompt, neither of which the server sequences. LOCALES: no translations/ directory, so gen:errors runs with ERRORS_LOCALES=ru, ERRORS_CATALOG_DIR pointed at stapel-core's catalogue and ERRORS_LOCALE_EXEMPT_OWNERS=stapel_geo - the 42 cross-cutting keys come from core in ru, the 8 geo keys are authored by the pair in its own ./i18n/ru until upstream localizes them. THE REFUSALS THIS PAIR IS SHAPED BY: 401/403 on the four geocoding verbs is the DEFAULT permission (GEOCODER_PERMISSIONS), so 'geocoding is not available to me' is a first-class state and NOT an error - the map renders and the pin drops for an anonymous visitor, only the address is missing; 429 is the server asking for quiet and keeps the last good suggestions on screen rather than replacing them with a red box; error.502.geocoder_unavailable is the one retryable failure, where every 400 is not; and a SUCCESSFUL call with zero features is an empty state (the middle of a lake has coordinates too), which is why nothing in the pair folds an empty answer into a failure.

This is the pin gen:rules copies the corpus from: tests/golden/rules/cases/ grows from 59 to 70 - both value ops on an unanswered controller, `not_in` on every empty payload shape and on a false bool, each effect's own default under an unmatched condition, and the any:[empty,not_in] spelling - and require-when-not-in-empty-value keeps its name while recording the opposite verdict (the corpus had pinned the defect). The generated imported set is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the bump: 3890 rules at both polarities, 7780 frames, 15730 expectations, zero divergence, because its polarity generator always answers the controller. || release v0.8.2 - 2026-09-02: IntConfig gains `optionsRef` — the vocabulary-backed allowed set for an integer (the year-of-make field scoped by the chosen generation): the value must be a term of the level, and with parentFeature filled, a child of the selected parent term; the value stays an int end to end and min/max keep applying as coarse bounds. $defs.IntConfig joins the canon (gated against the dataclass), which is what src/generated/featureDef.ts now emits IntConfig from. || release v0.8.1 - 2026-09-02: FeatureDef gains `visibility` (public/owner/staff) — which audience may READ a stored value, orthogonal to `mandatory`. src/generated/featureDef.ts was already emitting it and the pin was not; this is the pin that makes the generated canon true. release v0.7.1 - 2026-09-01: the generated rule corpus is source-neutral. The directory is tests/golden/rules/imported/ (was named after the source catalogue) and both files were regenerated with a synthetic option vocabulary (opt-001 / 'Option 1') and structural notes, with `expect` re-recorded from the live Python evaluator. This pin is what gen:rules copies from, so the bump and the driver's COPY_SET rename land together. 0.7.0 (also dragged in) snapshots the chosen options' `label` copy into SelectDao.labels. || release v0.6.1 - 2026-08-31: 0.6.0 plus the packaging fix it needed (the explicit [tool.setuptools] packages list had no stapel_attributes.types.group, so the published 0.6.0 wheel could not be imported at all). 0.6.0 is the composite `group` kind - one feature holding a small TABLE (config {type:'group', fields:[FeatureDef...], repeat:{min,max}|null}, DTO value a list of rows keyed by child slug, DAO rows whose cells are the children's own DAOs with their DaoMeta). stapel-vocabularies.note: release v0.2.0 - 2026-09-03: the popular band and a match that can say no. The term row carries band ("popular"|"all") and the page carries popular_count — how many LEADING rows are in the band. Both pairs on this contract now read them: @stapel/vocabularies-react forwards the page instead of projecting rows into a bare array, and @stapel/attributes-react renders the two bands in its picker. The split is a SLICE at popular_count, never a filter on the tag: under a query the server orders by prefix_rank first, so a popular-tagged row can legitimately sit after an all-tagged one and filtering would silently reorder the typeahead. release v0.1.0 - 2026-08-30: the NEW L2 module @stapel/vocabularies-react is the pair of, and the reason it exists. A ref feature carries a POINTER to a vocabulary level rather than an options list, because the lists do not fit in a category schema (529 phone vendors, 14962 models), so the terms arrive over a second wire this module serves. What is read here: docs/schema.json (4 paths under /vocabularies/api/v1/, 4 component schemas - Vocabulary, Level, Term, TermPage; the two the pair is built on are GET vocabularies/{slug}/terms/ (level, parent, q, limit, offset -> {results, total}) and GET vocabularies/{slug}/terms/resolve/ (level, codes -> {code: label}, unknown codes omitted)), docs/errors.json, docs/flows.json (literally [] - the module annotates no @flow_step, the stapel-categories precedent) and pyproject.toml 0.1.0 -> backend.contract >=0.1 <0.2. LOCALES: no translations/ directory, so gen:errors runs with ERRORS_CATALOG_DIR pointed at stapel-core's catalogue and ERRORS_LOCALE_EXEMPT_OWNERS=stapel_vocabularies - the cross-cutting keys come from core in ru/es, the module's own three (vocabulary_not_found, level_not_found, bad_parent) are authored by the pair in its own ./i18n/<locale> until upstream localizes them.
